text: Beyond annulus sizing, 75 of the 89 risk hearts fail due to R3_stj_oversize when the sinotubular junction is too narrow relative to the selected valve. Profiling 20 hearts in this failure group shows a lower mean stj_ratio of 1.09 compared to 1.21 for the rest of the cohort, and a mean stj of 25.8 mm versus 29.09 mm. Most failures cluster in the 1-1.1 (45 hearts) and 1.1-1.2 (48 hearts) stj_ratio bands.

Another 17 of the 89 risk hearts fail rule R2_sinus_clearance because the sinus of Valsalva lacks sufficient clearance for the assigned valve size. These 17 hearts have a markedly smaller mean sinus measurement of 28.73 mm compared to 33.54 mm across the remaining test hearts, despite having a comparable mean annulus of 22.82 mm versus 24.18 mm.

A total of 34 hearts result in noFit under R1_annulus_out_of_range because the design only covers annulus diameters from 21 mm to 29 mm. A profiled sample of 20 failing hearts has a mean annulus of 21.53 mm versus 24.26 mm for the rest. This includes hearts below 21 mm—such as 7 hearts in the 16-18 mm and 18-20 mm bands with a mean annulus of 19.02 mm—and hearts above 29 mm, where 5 failing hearts in the 28-30 mm and 30-32 mm bands have a mean annulus of 29.78 mm.

text: Out of 400 total test hearts, 75 hearts result in noFit due to R1_annulus_out_of_range because the design only covers annulus diameters from 21 to 27. Failing hearts fall outside this range in bands such as 16-18, 18-20, 20-22, 26-28, 28-30, and 30-32, with a profiled sample of 20 failing hearts showing a group mean annulus of 25.15 compared to 24.07 for the rest.

A group of 69 hearts fail under rule R3_stj_oversize because the valve is oversized relative to a narrow sinotubular junction. In a profiled sample of 20 hearts from this group, the mean stj is 25.45 compared to 29.11 in the rest of the test hearts, and the mean stj_ratio is 1.09 compared to 1.2 in the rest.

A group of 17 hearts fail under rule R2_sinus_clearance due to insufficient sinus dimensions relative to the selected valve size. Profiling all 17 hearts in this group reveals a mean sinus measurement of 28.73 compared to 33.54 in all other test hearts.
